laws.name: Network Act (Information and Communications Network Act)
laws.summary: The sector-specific statute governing online service providers. It carried Korea's data-protection rules for online users before PIPA existed, and hosted the real-name provisions.

laws.name: Game Industry Act premises restriction
laws.summary: Under-19s barred from gaming venues between 22:00 and 09:00. Survived the Shutdown Law's repeal and still applies.

laws.name: Real-name verification system
laws.summary: Sites above a traffic threshold had to verify the legal identity of anyone posting.

laws.name: Personal Information Protection Act
laws.summary: Enacted 30 September 2011 as a general data-protection law covering almost every organisation including government. Among the strictest regimes in the world, with criminal as well as regulatory penalties.

laws.name: Shutdown Law (Cinderella Law)
laws.summary: Under-16s blocked from online game servers between midnight and 6am. Korea was the first country to attempt a national gaming curfew.

laws.name: Data 3 Act amendments
laws.summary: Amendments to PIPA, the Network Act and the Credit Information Act came into force on 5 August 2020, introducing pseudonymised data and consolidating oversight under an independent commission.

laws.name: Personal Information Protection Commission made independent
laws.summary: Advisory since 2011, the commission became an independent regulator in 2020 with powers to investigate breaches and levy fines up to 3% of annual revenue.

laws.name: In-app payment law (Telecommunications Business Act amendment)
laws.summary: Barred app market operators from forcing developers onto their own billing systems. Passed 180 votes to 8 and nicknamed the Anti-Google law; the first such curb anywhere in the world.

laws.name: Parental choice system
laws.summary: Replaced the blanket curfew with per-family time limits set by guardians.

laws.name: In-app payment enforcement decree
laws.summary: KCC guidelines set the threshold at operators with at least 100 billion won in prior-year sales and a million daily users, which captures both Google and Apple.

laws.name: PIPA amendments of 2023
laws.summary: Effective 15 September 2023. Added data portability and the right to be excluded from automated decision-making, tightened overseas transfer rules, and replaced some criminal sanctions with fines.

laws.name: PIPA amendments of 2026
laws.summary: Amended 10 March 2026, with most provisions taking effect on 11 September 2026.

rulings.summary: Unanimous. The Court found the public benefit too small to justify the restriction on expression, and noted users had simply migrated to foreign sites.
The curfew survived constitutional challenge and ran for another seven years before being repealed politically rather than judicially.
Found it reasonable that Netflix provide something in return for network service. Appealed, then withdrawn on settlement in September 2023.

breaches.summary: Roughly 35 million accounts exposed, in a country of about 49 million people.
A routing error cut service to 16.5 million customers for about forty minutes.
